validator: draft 1 passes: ok true, no problems, no soft problems, no warnings. whatAmILookingAt is 11858 characters, close to the 12000 limit, so trim it to leave room for the fact-check's fixes.
keep: The idea is named up front: one shared flux, so every turn gets the same volts and the volts follow the turns; the supply holds the flux, so the primary cancels the secondary's ampere-turns, the amps go the other way and power in equals power out.

The picture is the brief's turns ratio: one core, two windings with turns sliders, a load switch and slider, a volts-per-turn tick the same on both windings, current bars moving the other way, equal power-in and power-out bars, a balancing ampere-turns line, a box showing the load as the 440 V side sees it, and a flux bar that stays put under load.

One rule set computes every figure: 0.5 V per turn = 440 / 880; V2 = 0.5 x N2; flux = 440 / (4.44 x 60 x N1) from lesson 3 (1.88 and 1.50 mWb); I2 = V2 / R; I1 = N2 I2 / N1; seen R = 440 / I1 = R (N1/N2)^2. 115 V, 23 A, 6.01 A, 5290 At, 2645 W, 73.2 ohm, 11.5 and 3.01 A, 29.3 ohm and 15.03 A all follow.

The causal step for the amps is there: the secondary's ampere-turns push against the change (Lenz, lesson 3), the flux must still make 440 V in the primary (lesson 3), so the primary draws just enough to cancel them. Power in = power out is then derived from the two ratios, not stated bare.

Both misconceptions the brief names have a DO screen with a hint per slip: OCR's 'step-down decreases the current' (screen 5, slip 153.04 A) and Lenz and Schmidt's 'higher load current saturates the core' (screen 9, slip 3.76 mWb). Ratio-once versus ratio-squared is caught on screens 11 and 12.

The recall opener the brief sets (Complex numbers lesson 7, the size of 3 + j4) is screen 1, typed, with 'Still there.', and it pays off in mixed puzzle 12: a complex load scaled by a real factor keeps its angle.
Typed answers for every figure (screens 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13) with want, slips and hints; options only on screen 12, whose answer is an expression.

The isolating point the brief gives lesson 4 is one sentence: the windings share only flux, no wire joins them, so the secondary is a circuit of its own. Losses, regulation, three-phase and the CT are left to lessons 5 to 8.
Every SHOW screen is under 90 words (82, 79, 81, 78, 77); every DO Read only restates its question; every SHOW has a Read and a Still. Three footnotes on screens and four sources in all.
fix: False absolute in explain: 'The supply holds that flux, so a load cannot move it.' A real load moves the flux a very little (the ignores says so). Say a load barely moves it.

Explain's closing paragraph chains three clauses round a footnote ('needs a small magnetising current, loses a little power, as little as 1% in a good one, and its output sags'). Split into short sentences.
Analogy: 'from a gearbox you have taken apart' presumes; say 'in a gearbox'. 'Torque times speed is the same on both shafts' needs 'less a little friction' to stay true.
Breaks: 'a transformer passes nothing on DC' is too absolute, since a switched DC gives a kick while the current changes (lesson 3). Say nothing on steady DC.

Screen 5's hint for 153.04 says 'steps the current down with the volts', which describes the wrong side. The slip makes the 115 V side's current the smaller; say that, and that a step-down raises the current.
Screen 13's hint for 0.6 says the current 'steps down as the volts go up', but 0.6 A on the 115 V side means the current rises with the volts. Reword: the higher-voltage side carries less current.
Trim whatAmILookingAt by a few hundred characters (repeated words in the picture and rules paragraphs) to leave room under 12000.
shape: Idea in one line up front: yes. Rule in words: yes (volts follow turns; ampere-turns balance; power in = power out; load seen times ratio squared). One worked example with real numbers: the 880/230 turn, 440 V to 115 V, 5 ohm case through explain, and the 10 kVA case in practice. Misconception shown failing: step-down current (screen 5) and load saturating the core (screens 8, 9). Trade analogy with where it breaks: meshed gears (torque follows teeth as volts follow turns), new to this course. Put it into practice: safe way first, steps, rules of thumb, worked example, mistakes. Recap: the bold takeaway and the finish screen.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with the seven fixes; no structural change.
